name: Multi-Branch nftables + QoS Lab
summary: A company with offices in Ankara, Istanbul and London, an academic branch of 10,000 students plus teachers and staff, and a software team. One Linux machine is the central firewall/router: default-drop nftables policy, an access matrix between groups, and tc HTB classes that share a 1 Gbit uplink (software 250-600, students 250-500, teachers/staff/offices 100-300 Mbit).

chosen.reason: Stateful default-drop filtering, NAT, packet marking and tc HTB QoS on one box; reproducible and testable with nmap/iperf3.

alternatives.reason: Web UI and plugins for the same job; heavier than a single script. (Reviewer-added comparison; not in the student's original submission.)
Classic open-source firewall with traffic shaper and VPN. (Reviewer-added comparison; not in the student's original submission.)
Commercial NGFW appliance, IPS and SD-WAN, for a real deployment. (Reviewer-added comparison; not in the student's original submission.)
Small-office appliance with easy UI and synchronized endpoint protection. (Reviewer-added comparison; not in the student's original submission.)

rules.note: Replies to established connections must pass or nothing works (stateful tracking).
Students reach no internal network (staff, software, offices).
Students get web (80/443, QUIC 443) and DNS only.
Teachers are blocked from the student and staff networks.
Teachers get web, mail and video conferencing (Teams/Zoom ports) to the internet.
Staff reach the offices for administrative work.
Software team is the most privileged group and reaches everything.
Offices reach the software team only on SSH, web and 8080.
The firewall itself accepts SSH only from the software and Ankara networks.
DNS and DHCP (53, 67/udp) are served to internal networks only.
Default rule: everything else is logged (rate-limited) and dropped.

remoteAccess.note: Inter-branch links are assumed to be VPN (WireGuard for London is on the roadmap); SSH to the firewall only from the software and Ankara networks.

monitoring.siem: nftables counters and rate-limited kernel log prefixes (FW-INPUT-DROP, FW-FWD-DROP) read with journalctl; Prometheus/Grafana and Wazuh/Graylog are on the roadmap.
monitoring.owner: The lab operator who runs company_fw.sh reviews the drop counters and logs; no 24/7 owner exists in the original design.
monitoring.alertSink: journald on the firewall host (Alertmanager planned).
monitoring.appVsSecurity: Not separated yet; QoS class counters (tc -s class) cover bandwidth while FW-* log prefixes cover security events.
